hero.description: The Chapel of Nuestro Padre Jesús del Prendimiento is the titular chapel of the Californios confraternity, and is located on one side of the Church of Santa María de Gracia in Cartagena (Spain). It was built in 1760 and houses some of the sculptures with which the confraternity replaced those destroyed during the Spanish Civil War: the sculptural group of the Arrest of Jesus (Mariano Benlliure, 1942), the Santísima Virgen del Primer Dolor (Benlliure, 1946), Saint John the Evangelist (Benlliure, 1946), the group of the Kiss of Judas (originally created by Francisco Salzillo in 1761, and its missing figures replaced by Benlliure in 1946), the group of the Samaritan woman at the well (José Sánchez Lozano, 1945), the Santísimo Cristo de la Flagelación (Benlliure, 1947), part of the group of the Agony in the Garden (Sánchez Lozano, 1974) and Saint Peter the Apostle (Sánchez Lozano, 1940).

gallery.description: The Church of Santa María de Gracia in Cartagena, Spain. The temple, built between 1716 and 1798 but consegrated already in 1779, is the center of the religious Holy Week events in the city. After severe damages in 1873 during the Cantonal rebellion it was restored in 1880, and again in the current Baroque Revival style by Lorenzo Ros Costa in 1943, after being target of attacks in 1936 during the Spanish Civil War. In fact, the demolition of the church was even approved by the Republicans but it did not eventually occur. The high altar depicted in the picture hosts the Chapel of the Four Saints (Leander, Fulgentius, Florentina and Isidore), along with the Virgin of Rosell in the middle.

gallery.title: File:Virgen del Rosell (20240712 092807).jpg
gallery.description: The Virgin of Rosell, a Romanesque Madonna and Child sculpture traditionally dated to the 13th century that is worshipped in the Church of Santa María de Gracia in Cartagena, Spain. The photograph corresponds to the part behind the altar in said temple, where the sculpture is located under the shelter of a baldachin.

gallery.description: Saint Leander, a Baroque sculpture made by Francisco Salzillo in 1755 that is worshipped in the Church of Santa María de Gracia in Cartagena (Spain). The sculpture is part of the group of the Four Saints of Cartagena.

gallery.title: File:Cristo de Lepanto (20240712 092738).jpg
gallery.description: The Christ of Lepanto, an ivory carving dating from the 16th century that is worshipped in the presbytery of the Church of Santa María de Gracia in Cartagena (Spain). Traditionally it has been considered that it belonged to Admiral John of Austria, and that it was donated by him to Cartagena upon his return from the Battle of Lepanto.
